title: August 5 recap: Northwest Indiana news you may have missed today
text:
• Students at Crown Point High School surpassed state averages on Advanced Placement tests across 21 subjects in 2026.
• Country music, monster trucks, and rodeos are coming to Crown Point at the Lake County Fair starting on Friday.
• Workers in Northwest Indiana make more than the average in the rest of the state, but the Calumet Region's economic growth has been slowing down over the last two years.
• Police responded to a trailer park in Gary after receiving a report of an elderly man hanging out with two young children.
• Pete Crow-Armstrong hit two homers and a double to help the Chicago Cubs complete a three-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
• A crash occurred between 137th Avenue and U.S. 231 at around 4:22 p.m.
• A Target store under construction in Portage will bring the city seven new businesses, including Ross, Burlington, and TJ Maxx big-box stores.
• A Gary woman was accused of throwing hot grease during a violent domestic dispute.
• A test is available to learn about the Indiana gas tax and a loophole to extend its suspension."

Here’s a roundup of news and notables from Day 8 of Chicago Bears training camp, featuring T.J. Edwards’ return from injury and Darnell Wright’s first comments after his contract extension.
